_: Vitreous humour: a clear hyaluronan-collagen gel (~99 % water) filling the back ~80 % of the globe (~4 mL). Holds the intraocular pressure that keeps the shell taut: IOP is a world/state value carried here. Adult; liquefies with age. Eye-and-hair materials lane, 2026-11-07.

alpha.src: no free surface in the eye

F0.src: index-matched to the aqueous; no visible boundary

kinetic.src: not applicable: bonded at the vitreous base; elsewhere lies on the retina

viscosity_mPa_s.src: not a Newtonian number: viscoelastic gel (deform); liquefied vitreous behaves near water

phase.src: a very soft gel: solve as a viscoelastic fluid/MPM continuum, incompressible, filling the globe

collision_thickness_mm.src: fills its cavity; no gap to the retina

model.v: incompressible: pressure projection; carries the IOP

response_time_ms.src: vitreous after-movement following a saccade lasts ~0.1-1 s (clinical observation of floaters, recalled); E: recalled, not re-read

wave_speed_m_s.src: sqrt(G'/rho) with G' 6.5 Pa (TRAM18): ~8 cm/s - why floaters swirl slowly; sound ~ water

storage_modulus_Pa.src: TRAM18 (human n 23); lit range from its table

volume_mL.src: ~80 % of the 6.5 mL globe (EYEMD A4 textbook)

iop.src: RECALL population IOP (Colton & Ederer; diurnal swing recalled), not reopened: a WORLD/STATE value the solver applies as the globe's internal pressure

ageing.v: liquefies with age (gel fraction falls); G' and G'' fall

note.v: MPM/SPH viscoelastic with G' 6.5 Pa, or simply a pressure (IOP) + volume constraint on the shell
